name: Ben Thanh Market
kicker: The clock tower on Quách Thị Trang
summary: Bến Thành is the central hall on the square where Metro Line 1’s Bến Thành station sits. Vietnam Tourism says the aisles sell fresh produce, conical hats, weasel coffee, and lacquerware, and that the end of the hall cooks bánh xèo and assembles bánh mì. Vietnam Tourism says entry is free, inside a clock it repeats on other sights. Hours and any door fee are Check on arrival.
fee: Vietnam Tourism says entry is free. Check on arrival.
getThere: Walk in the center. The metro station is the same square.
heroCaption: The clock tower and the name Chợ Bến Thành, from the square

notice.title: Bình Tây is a different hall
notice.body: Do not use Bến Thành’s free line or its clock for Chợ Bình Tây. The pages that name them put the halls in different districts.

body: Vietnam Tourism’s address is 32-30 Phan Bội Châu, Ben Thanh, District 1, facing Quách Thị Trang Square, on land Vietnam Tourism calls the former Bờ Rệt pond. The metro project places the station Bến Thành at Quảng trường Quách Thị Trang.

The tower photograph is the front you see from the square. The second photograph is an aisle of souvenirs and a jewelry case. It is not the food stalls. Those stalls, bánh xèo and bánh mì, are on the food guide. Agree a figure before you pay for anything in the hall. No stall price was printed.

figures.caption: An aisle of souvenirs and a jewelry case, not the food stalls
figures.alt: Souvenir aisle inside Ben Thanh Market

gettingThere: Walk from Nguyễn Huệ or the cathedral square. The metro station is on the same square, on Line 1.

legs.heading: By metro
legs.body: Line 1, station Bến Thành, at Quảng trường Quách Thị Trang. The 2024 fare in the opening article is not a 2026 price. Check the board.

hours: Check on arrival. Vietnam Tourism prints 7:30 a.m.–12 p.m. and 1:30–5 p.m. on this market and on several other sights. That split clock is not chosen.
closed: A weekly closing day was not printed once the repeated clock is set aside.
admissionNote: Vietnam Tourism says entry is free. Check on arrival.
